{"id": "2:185/q16", "question": "Why is guidance stated twice with clear proofs and criterion?", "turns_on": "Emphatic specification, distinct kinds of guidance, anaphora, or wider divine guidance.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q16/p1", "position": "The second phrase specifies or intensifies the first general guidance.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshaf and Razi read general then manifest best guidance; Bursevi calls it an honorific three-level description."}, {"id": "2:185/q16/p2", "position": "The two mentions distinguish fundamentals from derivative rulings.", "reasons": "Razi reports this way to avoid repetition; al-Samin reports it too."}, {"id": "2:185/q16/p3", "position": "The definite second huda points back to the first.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya argues from Arabic definite repetition; Abu Hayyan and al-Samin reject circular qualification."}, {"id": "2:185/q16/p4", "position": "The second huda and furqan are broader divine categories that include prior revelation.", "reasons": "Abu Hayyan and al-Samin prefer taking the Qur'an's guidance as one part of God's wider guidance and criterion."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q17", "question": "How are 'guidance' and 'clear signs' parsed?", "turns_on": "Their relation to the passive verb and to one another.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q17/p1", "position": "Both are accusative circumstantial descriptions of the Qur'an.", "reasons": "Al-Nahhas, Ibn Atiyya, and Abu Hayyan treat bayyinat as coordinated with hudan; al-Baghawi calls the indefinite hudan separated from definite Qur'an."}, {"id": "2:185/q17/p2", "position": "Hudan supplies a second object or an accusative after the verb's passive subject.", "reasons": "Al-Wahidi calls it guiding and connects it to anzala; al-Akhfash compares a verb already occupied by its first object."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q18", "question": "What role does the fa before 'whoever witnesses' play?", "turns_on": "Conditional consequence or allegedly surplus connective.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q18/p1", "position": "It marks a conditional consequence of Ramadan's distinction or the subject-predicate relation.", "reasons": "Abu Ali and Razi explain that the month of revelation warrants a special worship; Razi cites 62:8 for a parallel."}, {"id": "2:185/q18/p2", "position": "It is extra in a predicate, with no true conditional function.", "reasons": "Al-Akhfash and al-Mazini cite 62:8 and poetry; Razi and Abu Hayyan argue against the analogy."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q19", "question": "What does witnessing the month mean and how is al-shahr construed?", "turns_on": "Presence in town, reaching the period, certain knowledge, or crescent sighting; object versus time adverb.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q19/p1", "position": "Being resident and present during Ramadan; al-shahr is a time adverb.", "reasons": "Tabari, Wahidi and most grammarians omit the object 'town'; travelers too encounter Ramadan, so literal month-as-object cannot by itself mean residence."}, {"id": "2:185/q19/p2", "position": "Reaching or knowingly experiencing Ramadan, with the month as object.", "reasons": "Razi prefers this over omitted object by a principle favoring specification over ellipsis; Tabatabai denies that this phrase itself requires residence or moon sighting."}, {"id": "2:185/q19/p3", "position": "It means observing the crescent or knowing its arrival with certainty.", "reasons": "Baydawi proposes seeing the crescent; Alusi says its certainty triggers fasting; Abu Hayyan and Ibn Ashur object to identifying shahida with seeing."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q20", "question": "If Ramadan begins while one is resident, may one later travel and break the fast?", "turns_on": "Whether witnessing the beginning binds the whole month or the travel exception applies to later days.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q20/p1", "position": "No; residence at the month's start obliges the full fast despite later travel.", "reasons": "Ali, Ubayda, al-Suddi and others argue that witnessing the beginning covers the month; Razi reads the whole for a part."}, {"id": "2:185/q20/p2", "position": "Yes; one fasts resident days and may use the concession after travel begins.", "reasons": "Tabari and Qurtubi prefer this based on the Prophet fasting then breaking during the conquest journey; the exception qualifies the general command."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q21", "question": "Who becomes obligated when Ramadan arrives, including those gaining legal capacity midmonth?", "turns_on": "Legal capacity at entry versus duties beginning only when capacity or Islam begins.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q21/p1", "position": "The obligation presupposes Islam, adulthood, reason, health, and awareness of Ramadan; later entrants owe remaining days.", "reasons": "Jishumi and Qurtubi apply the command to responsible believers; Qurtubi says conversion after dawn does not impose prior days and prefers no make-up for that day."}, {"id": "2:185/q21/p2", "position": "Legal capacity during any part can obligate make-up of insanity days, but insanity throughout excuses.", "reasons": "Abu Hanifa and companions distinguish entire-month insanity from recovery during the month; al-Shafi'i requires only days after recovery."}, {"id": "2:185/q21/p3", "position": "A convert also makes up earlier Ramadan days.", "reasons": "Ata and al-Hasan require past days; Qurtubi argues that the earlier address was not yet directed to the convert."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q22", "question": "How is Ramadan's start and end established?", "turns_on": "Crescent sighting or completing thirty days versus astronomical calculation, and how daytime sightings count.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q22/p1", "position": "Sight the crescent, or complete the preceding month to thirty if obscured.", "reasons": "Prophetic reports from Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayra; Qurtubi says this gives certainty and rejects calculation as a primary standard; Elmalili links it to 2:189."}, {"id": "2:185/q22/p2", "position": "Lunar stations or calculation can establish an obscured month.", "reasons": "Mutarrif and Ibn Qutayba read 'estimate it' astronomically; Kuran Yolu endorses visibility-based calendar calculations checked by observatories."}, {"id": "2:185/q22/p3", "position": "A crescent seen during Ramadan's thirtieth day belongs to the coming night.", "reasons": "Qurtubi cites Aisha's fast until evening and the majority; al-Thawri's noon split is contrary."}, {"id": "2:185/q22/p4", "position": "A crescent seen before noon belongs to the preceding night; after noon to the coming night.", "reasons": "Al-Thawri and Abu Yusuf cite reports from Umar and Ali, but Abu Umar disputes the connectedness of the supporting report."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q23", "question": "Whose crescent testimony suffices?", "turns_on": "One versus two witnesses, clear versus obscured sky, and private observation.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q23/p1", "position": "One upright observer can establish Ramadan; Shawwal generally needs two.", "reasons": "Al-Shafi'i's early view and Abu Hanifa cite Ibn Umar's report; Razi and Elmalili distinguish Ramadan precaution and the human interests of Eid."}, {"id": "2:185/q23/p2", "position": "Two upright witnesses are needed for Ramadan too.", "reasons": "Malik analogizes Shawwal and Dhu al-Hijja; al-Shafi'i's later position agrees."}, {"id": "2:185/q23/p3", "position": "With a clear sky, numerous observers are needed; obstruction permits one for Ramadan, two for Eid.", "reasons": "Elmalili explains the Hanafi concern that a few claims conflict with many careful observers under clear skies."}, {"id": "2:185/q23/p4", "position": "A lone observer follows the personal sighting for both months.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Mundhir says both fasting and breaking bind the lone observer; Malik instead says fast personally but do not break on Shawwal."}, {"id": "2:185/q23/p5", "position": "A lone observer follows neither sighting without communal proof.", "reasons": "Ata and Ishaq hold this."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q24", "question": "Does a crescent sighting in one region bind another?", "turns_on": "Different horizons and local Prophetic practice versus a shared public ruling.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q24/p1", "position": "Distant localities use their own sightings; neighboring districts may share.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas rejects Syria's earlier sighting for Medina in Kurayb's report; Ibn al-Arabi prefers the horizon explanation."}, {"id": "2:185/q24/p2", "position": "A proven sighting elsewhere obliges other localities, with make-up if learned later.", "reasons": "Al-Layth and al-Shafi'i are cited; Malik's Basra-to-Yemen report and Ibn al-Majishun distinguish widespread proof from judge-bound testimony."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q25", "question": "How is the command lam in 'let him fast' read?", "turns_on": "Sukun after fa versus preserving original kasra, with a reported dialectal fatḥa.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q25/p1", "position": "The common reading makes the command lam vowelless after fa.", "reasons": "Al-Hasan and others preserve kasra; grammarians explain the lightening after fa, waw or thumma."}, {"id": "2:185/q25/p2", "position": "Al-Hasan, al-A'raj and others read it with kasra.", "reasons": "The kasra is original to isolated command lam and permissible in connected speech."}, {"id": "2:185/q25/p3", "position": "A dialectal open lam is reported.", "reasons": "Al-Farra associates it with Banu Sulaym, especially before an open following vowel."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q26", "question": "What is a valid Ramadan fast and what invalidates it?", "turns_on": "Intention, abstention, endpoint, and accidental or forgetful acts.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q26/p1", "position": "A fast needs intention and knowing abstention from food, drink, sex and other invalidators from dawn to sunset.", "reasons": "Razi invokes Prophetic statements on intentions and sunset; Ibn al-Jawzi distinguishes lexical abstention from the legal fast."}, {"id": "2:185/q26/p2", "position": "Abstention alone suffices without a separate intention.", "reasons": "

Some reported by Razi reason that the command is fulfilled by refraining."}, {"id": "2:185/q26/p3", "position": "Forgetful eating or drinking does not invalidate the fast.", "reasons": "Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i hold this; Elmalili cites a report calling the forgetful lapse God's hospitality."}, {"id": "2:185/q26/p4", "position": "Forgetful eating or drinking invalidates the fast.", "reasons": "Malik is reported to hold this."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q27", "question": "Does this verse abrogate an earlier fasting or fidya ruling?", "turns_on": "Whether 2:183-184 described a former option or one coherent Ramadan rule.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q27/p1", "position": "It ends the healthy resident's former choice of fasting or feeding.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas, Salama and the majority report an earlier choice; Ibn Kathir says the elderly unable to fast retain feeding. Razi notes this would replace a lighter rule with a heavier one."}, {"id": "2:185/q27/p2", "position": "The fasting verses form one discourse and do not abrogate one another.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur and Tabatabai read shahr as explaining counted days; Bint al-Shati and Kuran Yolu distinguish fidya for the unable from make-up for temporary excuses."}, {"id": "2:185/q27/p3", "position": "The earlier counted days were a separate three-day or Ashura fast later replaced by Ramadan.", "reasons": "Elmalili reports Qatada, Ata and Muadh; the majority instead identify the counted days with Ramadan."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q28", "question": "Why is the illness and travel concession repeated?", "turns_on": "Preserving a concession after a changed rule versus completing a single staged explanation.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q28/p1", "position": "It confirms the exemption remains after the resident's former fidya choice ends.", "reasons": "Mawardi, Wahidi, Ibn al-Jawzi and Biqai say otherwise the new command could seem to remove every earlier option."}, {"id": "2:185/q28/p2", "position": "It restates the operative rule at its natural place after the month is specified.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur says the prior mention reassured listeners in advance; Tabatabai treats earlier verses as preparation, not enacted alternatives."}, {"id": "2:185/q28/p3", "position": "It specifies the general fasting command by excluding excused cases.", "reasons": "Qurtubi says the later qualification limits the earlier general obligation; Alusi notes that under a residence reading only illness newly needs exception."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q29", "question": "What illness permits postponing the fast?", "turns_on": "Any named illness, inability to pray standing, intolerable worsening, or personal strength.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q29/p1", "position": "Any condition that is called illness qualifies.", "reasons": "Ibn Sirin's painful finger illustrates the view; Zahiris and al-Hasan in Jishumi invoke the wording's unrestricted label."}, {"id": "2:185/q29/p2", "position": "An illness that prevents standing for prayer qualifies.", "reasons": "Ibrahim and al-Hasan use standing prayer as their threshold."}, {"id": "2:185/q29/p3", "position": "Fasting must likely cause intolerable harm, worsening or exhaustion.", "reasons": "Al-Shafi'i and most jurists favor this; al-Tabari phrases it as hardship beyond capacity, otherwise the duty remains."}, {"id": "2:185/q29/p4", "position": "The person assesses weakness: break if weak, fast if strong.", "reasons": "Al-Sadiq's report through Abu Basir leaves assessment to the patient regardless of illness label."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q30", "question": "What journey qualifies for the concession?", "turns_on": "Any travel versus stated distances and the kinds of journeys accepted.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q30/p1", "position": "Any journey, short or long, qualifies.", "reasons": "Dawud follows the unrestricted word; Razi rejects inferring a three-day minimum from the footwear-wiping report."}, {"id": "2:185/q30/p2", "position": "About two days or sixteen farsakhs qualifies.", "reasons": "Al-Shafi'i and Wahidi give sixteen farsakhs; Razi cites the Mecca-to-Asfan four-station report."}, {"id": "2:185/q30/p3", "position": "Three days' journey qualifies.", "reasons": "Abu Hanifa and al-Thawri's school use this threshold; Abu Hanifa cites consensus and a three-day footwear-wiping allowance."}, {"id": "2:185/q30/p4", "position": "Eight farsakhs on a permitted or devotional journey qualifies.", "reasons": "Tabrisi reports the Imami rule and contrasts al-Shafi'i's sixteen and Abu Hanifa's twenty-four farsakhs."}, {"id": "2:185/q30/p5", "position": "A one-day journey suffices.", "reasons": "Baghawi reports this additional distance."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q31", "question": "When a resident departs during a fasting day, may that day's fast be broken?", "turns_on": "Whether the travel status can change an obligation already begun after dawn.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q31/p1", "position": "No; one who began the day resident completes that day.", "reasons": "Most scholars in Baghawi, and Zuhri, Malik, Shafi'i, Awza'i and Abu Hanifa in Ibn Ashur hold this; if broken, make-up is due."}, {"id": "2:185/q31/p2", "position": "Yes, after actual departure the traveler may break even that day.", "reasons": "Ahmad, Ishaq and al-Sha'bi hold this; Ibn Ashur prefers it from Anas's practice and Ibn Abbas's conquest report."}, {"id": "2:185/q31/p3", "position": "Breaking that day also incurs expiation.", "reasons": "Ibn Kinanah and al-Makhzumi reason from the obligation begun at home; Ibn Abd al-Barr rejects expiation because travel is an explicit license."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q32", "question": "May one set out on a journey after Ramadan has begun?", "turns_on": "Advice to remain home versus ordinary permission to travel.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q32/p1", "position": "One should stay or defer discretionary travel.", "reasons": "Aisha, Ubayda and Ibrahim advise waiting; al-Sadiq excepts Hajj, umra or urgent livelihood, and Tabatabai treats this as recommended."}, {"id": "2:185/q32/p2", "position": "Travel remains permitted during Ramadan.", "reasons": "Al-Hakam and Hammad tell a traveler to go; al-Hasan says Ramadan does not restrain travel."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q33", "question": "Must an ill person or traveler break the fast, and does a fast then count?", "turns_on": "An assigned later fast versus an optional postponement of the Ramadan duty.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q33/p1", "position": "Breaking is a concession; a completed Ramadan fast is valid and needs no make-up.", "reasons": "Tabari and the majority cite the Prophet's fast and his permission to Hamza, and Abu Sa'id's report that fasters and non-fasters did not blame each other; Tabari limits 'not righteousness' to extreme strain."}, {"id": "2:185/q33/p2", "position": "Breaking is obligatory; fasting during illness or travel fails and must be made up.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas, Umar, Abu Hurayra and Ahl al-Bayt reports take the later-days clause as the appointed duty; Tabatabai rejects supplying an unstated 'if he breaks' and cites Imami reports."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q34", "question": "When both travel choices are valid, which is preferable?", "turns_on": "Fasting's immediacy, accepting the concession, equal liberty, or individual ease.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q34/p1", "position": "Fasting is generally better when it can be borne.", "reasons": "Anas and al-Shafi'i cite completing Ramadan with the community and Prophetic travel fasting."}, {"id": "2:185/q34/p2", "position": "Breaking is better because it accepts God's concession.", "reasons": "Ibn Umar likens the license to God's offered charity; reports warn against refusing it."}, {"id": "2:185/q34/p3", "position": "The preferable choice is whichever is easier in the circumstances.", "reasons": "Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Qasim compare the present journey with later make-up; the shaded traveler's extreme strain calls for breaking."}, {"id": "2:185/q34/p4", "position": "Both choices are equally permissible without a standing preference.", "reasons": "Hamza's Prophetic permission and companions' mutual non-criticism support this."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q35", "question": "What number of make-up days is due?", "turns_on": "Day-for-day count versus replacing a whole month irrespective of length.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q35/p1", "position": "Exactly the number of missed fast days, whether Ramadan had twenty-nine or thirty.", "reasons": "Tabari, Wahidi and al-Kiya stress the word 'number'; no make-up is owed for days actually fasted."}, {"id": "2:185/q35/p2", "position": "A whole month's make-up is due for a whole missed Ramadan, regardless of day count.", "reasons": "Hasan ibn Salih is reported to hold this; al-Kiya objects that the verse counts days."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q36", "question": "Must Ramadan make-up days be consecutive?", "turns_on": "Unrestricted count versus analogy with the original continuous month.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q36/p1", "position": "They may be consecutive or separate.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas, Anas and the majority rely on the unrestricted 'number of other days'; Aisha's sound report says 'consecutive' was dropped, understood as abrogation."}, {"id": "2:185/q36/p2", "position": "They must be consecutive, mirroring Ramadan.", "reasons": "Ibn Umar and a minority require succession; weak Prophetic reports support it, while al-Baji says Ibn Umar may only have recommended it."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q37", "question": "When must make-up fasting occur, and what if it is delayed or interrupted?", "turns_on": "Immediate performance, delay until next Ramadan, and expiation for delay or deliberate interruption.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q37/p1", "position": "It may be delayed until before the next Ramadan.", "reasons": "Aisha made up days in Sha'ban; Ibn Ashur and the majority see no immediate command. Tabrisi says the Imami school also allows delay within that period."}, {"id": "2:185/q37/p2", "position": "Make-up must begin promptly after the excuse ends.", "reasons": "Al

-Hasan and others require immediate make-up; Dawud specifies the day after Eid."}, {"id": "2:185/q37/p3", "position": "Delay beyond the next Ramadan brings fidya as well as make-up.", "reasons": "Tabrisi reports the Imami and Shafi'i rule."}, {"id": "2:185/q37/p4", "position": "Deliberately breaking a make-up fast requires no expiation.", "reasons": "The majority say Ramadan's sanctity, not mere replacement, grounds expiation."}, {"id": "2:185/q37/p5", "position": "Deliberately breaking a make-up fast requires expiation.", "reasons": "Qatada analogizes the replacement to the original worship."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q38", "question": "How is the phrase 'a number of other days' parsed?", "turns_on": "Omitted condition or predicate, and the agreement and declension of ukhar.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q38/p1", "position": "The clause omits 'if he breaks the fast'; idda is a nominative counted duty.", "reasons": "Jishumi compares 2:196; Qurtubi supplies an omitted predicate or siyam, while al-Kisai allows an imperative analysis."}, {"id": "2:185/q38/p2", "position": "Ukhar is the feminine plural of ukhra because plural days take feminine agreement.", "reasons": "Tabari compares kubra and qurba; Ibn Ashur argues this is lighter and more natural."}, {"id": "2:185/q38/p3", "position": "Ukhar is diptote because of adjectival displacement or its plural pattern.", "reasons": "Sibawayh and al-Kisai offer different morphological explanations; Ibn Ashur questions the usual account."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q39", "question": "Why is 'on a journey' coordinated with 'ill'?", "turns_on": "Prepositional phrase functioning like an adjective and the force of 'on'.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q39/p1", "position": "'On a journey' has the force of 'traveling' and can coordinate with 'ill'.", "reasons": "Tabari and Jishumi compare 10:12's coordinated bodily states; Ibn Ashur says 'on' requires actual ongoing travel, not mere intent."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q40", "question": "What ease and hardship does God intend or reject?", "turns_on": "Specific travel concession, general religious ease, or spiritual and final outcomes.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q40/p1", "position": "The illness and travel dispensation is ease; compelled fasting under those conditions is hardship.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Tabari identify breaking and later make-up; Muqatil calls the concession gentleness."}, {"id": "2:185/q40/p2", "position": "The statement covers ease throughout religion and life.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya and Qurtubi cite 22:78 and reports that religion is easy; Ibn Kathir adduces commands to make things easy."}, {"id": "2:185/q40/p3", "position": "It can mean Paradise through fasting and avoidance of Hell.", "reasons": "Al-Tirmidhi and al-Fadli interpret ease and hardship in terms of spiritual states and final abodes."}, {"id": "2:185/q40/p4", "position": "Ease may mean wilaya, hardship opposition to it.", "reasons": "Tabatabai treats this Imami report as an application rather than exclusive lexical meaning."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q41", "question": "What does divine willing in this verse imply theologically?", "turns_on": "Will as eternal attribute, command, or human freedom and capacity.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q41/p1", "position": "God's will is an eternal attribute; the verse can refer to His legal command for ease.", "reasons": "Qurtubi argues the ordered contingent world needs a willing creator; Razi answers Mu'tazilite universal readings by limiting ease to the fasting rulings or distinguishing command from will."}, {"id": "2:185/q41/p2", "position": "God does not will human hardship or impossible duties, supporting responsible human action.", "reasons": "Jishumi and Tabrisi use the wording against compulsion and the claim that God wills every hardship; the Mu'tazila challenge created human disbelief."}, {"id": "2:185/q41/p3", "position": "Here willing can mean requesting or commanding ease rather than determining every event.", "reasons": "Abu Hayyan notes that hardship occurs although Sunni doctrine says what God wills occurs; al-Muntakhab supplies 'command what contains ease'."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q42", "question": "How are yusr and usr read and what do they mean?", "turns_on": "Still versus rounded sin, with no substantive change.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q42/p1", "position": "The majority leave the sin still; Abu Ja'far and others give it damma.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya lists readers; Ibn Ashur explains vowel harmony; Qiraat-ER calls it phonetic without changed meaning."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q43", "question": "What does completing the count require?", "turns_on": "Making up missed days, full lunar Ramadan observance, or both.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q43/p1", "position": "Complete missed fasting days by make-up until the count equals Ramadan's duty.", "reasons": "Tabari, Dahhak and Ibn Zayd identify the missed number; al-Samin takes the article as anaphoric to the earlier idda."}, {"id": "2:185/q43/p2", "position": "Complete the lunar Ramadan itself, whether it has twenty-nine or thirty days.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas and Ata take the month as the count; sighting ends a twenty-nine-day month, clouds lead to thirty. Some instead argued it could never be shorter."}, {"id": "2:185/q43/p3", "position": "It includes both direct fasting during Ramadan and later make-up for excused days.", "reasons": "Razi says 'count' rather than 'month' accommodates both; Ibn Ashur ties number to the wisdom of a full month."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q44", "question": "How is litukmilū read?", "turns_on": "Light Form IV versus doubled Form II and their possible force.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q44/p1", "position": "Most read a light mim, from akmala.", "reasons": "Al-Farisi and Baghawi compare 5:3; al-Kisai prefers it, while other authorities say the two forms are synonymous."}, {"id": "2:185/q44/p2", "position": "Abu Bakr from Asim, Yaqub and some Abu Amr transmissions double mim.", "reasons": "Ibn Khalawayh hears repeated fasting through the month; Qiraat-ER hears meticulous completion; al-Farisi cites fa'ala/af'ala interchange and al-Nabigha."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q45", "question": "How is the purpose lam in 'so you complete' connected?", "turns_on": "Implied will, supplied purpose or action, direct object, extra waw, or independent imperative.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q45/p1", "position": "It continues 'God wills' with an understood purpose/object: He wills completion and magnification.", "reasons": "Al-Akhfash and Basrans supply an after lam; a cited 'I want to forget her' poem illustrates the construction."}, {"id": "2:185/q45/p2", "position": "The lam is purposive and an omitted act of granting ease governs it.", "reasons": "Al-Farra and Tabari infer 'He legislated or granted the concession'; 6:75 supplies an analogous omitted act."}, {"id": "2:185/q45/p3", "position": "It coordinates by meaning with an omitted earlier purpose, 'to make matters easy'.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjaj uses poetry to show coordination with the understood sense; al-Kashshaf favors an omitted purpose."}, {"id": "2:185/q45/p4", "position": "It is an imperative lam joining an independent command.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya reports this; Abu Hayyan and al-Samin object to its rare second-person form and uniform kasra."}, {"id": "2:185/q45/p5", "position": "The waw is superfluous and the lam depends directly on ease.", "reasons": "Al-Nahhas reports this; Abu Hayyan and al-Samin call it weak."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q46", "question": "What is meant by magnifying God here?", "turns_on": "General praise and greatness or the specific Eid practice.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q46/p1", "position": "Magnify and praise God for guidance, by remembrance and obedience.", "reasons": "Tabari mentions the religious guidance and ability to fast; al-Kashshaf gives general exaltation; Ibn Ashur explains Allahu akbar as God's unique majesty."}, {"id": "2:185/q46/p2", "position": "It refers specifically to Eid al-Fitr takbir at Ramadan's completion.", "reasons": "Sufyan, Zayd b. Aslam, Ibn Abbas and many jurists locate it at Eid, though details vary."}, {"id": "2:185/q46/p3", "position": "It refers to takbir at the appearance of the new moon.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshaf records this separate occasion."}, {"id": "2:185/q46/p4", "position": "It can embrace belief, speech and action as reverence for God's unique greatness.", "reasons": "Razi and Elmalili describe affirming names and attributes, inward assent, and worship, while Elmalili gives contextual priority to spoken Eid takbir."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q47", "question": "When should Eid al-Fitr takbir begin and end?", "turns_on": "Crescent, sunset, departure, imam's arrival, prayer, or sermon.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q47/p1", "position": "From sighting Shawwal's crescent through Eid prayer or sermon.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas reports variants ending at the imam's arrival, the sermon, or Eid's end; al-Shafi'i starts at sunset."}, {"id": "2:185/q47/p2", "position": "From leaving home for the prayer ground until the imam appears or prayer ends.", "reasons": "Zayd b. Aslam and Malik report this; an early departure may wait until sunrise. Ahmad's reports differ on whether the sermon ends it."}, {"id": "2:185/q47/p3", "position": "At specified Eid-night and Eid-day prayers.", "reasons": "Tabrisi gives Maghrib, Isha, dawn and Eid prayer; al-Sadiq's reports also include noon and afternoon, which Tabatabai treats as differing recommendation grades."}, {"id": "2:185/q47/p4", "position": "It belongs to Eid day, not necessarily the preceding night.", "reasons": "Sufyan and Malik give day-focused accounts; Malik and Ahmad are reported against Eid-night takbir."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q48", "question": "What takbir formula and public manner are prescribed?", "turns_on": "Fixed three repetitions versus varied formulas, audible or quiet recitation.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q48/p1", "position": "Three repetitions of Allahu akbar are the common formula.", "reasons": "Malik, Sha

fi'i, Abu Hanifa and a reported Jabir practice support it; Abu Hanifa requires the three."}, {"id": "2:185/q48/p2", "position": "Formulas may add oneness, praise and glorification; no fixed wording is required.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Mubarak and Ibn Masud offer longer versions; Malik, Ahmad and Ibn al-Arabi allow breadth."}, {"id": "2:185/q48/p3", "position": "Takbir should be audible in communal Eid practice.", "reasons": "Shafi'i, Malik and others commend raised voices at both Eids; reports from Ibn Umar and al-Sulami describe it."}, {"id": "2:185/q48/p4", "position": "At Fitr, quiet takbir is recommended en route; aloud is for Adha.", "reasons": "Elmalili gives the preferred Hanafi practice and says the verse itself does not impose loudness."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q49", "question": "Is Eid al-Fitr takbir obligatory, recommended, or unprescribed?", "turns_on": "The force of the verse's command and its Eid-specific interpretation.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q49/p1", "position": "It is recommended Sunnah.", "reasons": "Most scholars in Ibn Kathir infer its prescription without imposing duty; Ata calls it Sunnah."}, {"id": "2:185/q49/p2", "position": "It is obligatory from the verse's apparent command.", "reasons": "Dawud al-Zahiri argues from the imperative."}, {"id": "2:185/q49/p3", "position": "It is not prescribed at Fitr.", "reasons": "Abu Hanifa is reported to restrict Eid takbir to Adha or dislike Fitr morning takbir; Elmalili's Hanafi presentation instead recommends it quietly."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q50", "question": "Why does takbir take 'upon what He guided you'?", "turns_on": "On as praise or cause, and ma as verbal noun or relative pronoun.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q50/p1", "position": "Takbir includes praising God, so 'upon' expresses praise for His guidance.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshaf and Nasafi give this semantic account; al-Samin prefers retaining the preposition's ordinary elevated sense; Abu Hayyan says syntactically takbir itself performs the praise."}, {"id": "2:185/q50/p2", "position": "'Upon' means 'because of' guidance.", "reasons": "Abu Hayyan and al-Burhan allow causal force."}, {"id": "2:185/q50/p3", "position": "Ma is a verbal noun: for His guiding you.", "reasons": "Abu Hayyan and al-Samin prefer it because a relative reading needs two omissions."}, {"id": "2:185/q50/p4", "position": "Ma is relative: for that to which He guided you.", "reasons": "Baydawi permits the construed object; Abu Hayyan says it may denote law or escape from Christian changes to fasting."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q51", "question": "What guidance is the cause for magnification?", "turns_on": "General religion, Ramadan fasting, wilaya, or contrast with other communities.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q51/p1", "position": "It is guidance to religion and its laws generally.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas and Ibn Atiyya favor this broad reference; Tabari adds enablement to fast."}, {"id": "2:185/q51/p2", "position": "It is guidance to Ramadan's fast and approved way of performing it.", "reasons": "Baghawi calls the fast this community's privilege; Mawardi reports this narrower referent."}, {"id": "2:185/q51/p3", "position": "It is guidance away from Christian alteration of fasting or pagan boasting.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya and Qurtubi report those historical contrasts."}, {"id": "2:185/q51/p4", "position": "It can be wilaya as one application of divine guidance.", "reasons": "A report through al-Barqi gives this identification, which Tabatabai calls an instance or ta'wil."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q52", "question": "For what and how are believers to give thanks?", "turns_on": "Guidance, concession, reward, and enacted rather than merely verbal gratitude.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q52/p1", "position": "Thank God for guidance, easy obligations, and His blessings.", "reasons": "Tabari names guidance and help; Mawardi gives guidance as one object; Ibn Kathir links thanks with obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions."}, {"id": "2:185/q52/p2", "position": "Thank Him particularly for the fast-breaking concession.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshaf and Nasafi pair gratitude with ease; Ibn Ashur includes charity and Eid celebration as enacted thanks."}, {"id": "2:185/q52/p3", "position": "Thank Him for the reward granted to obedience.", "reasons": "Mawardi gives this as a separate object of gratitude."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q53", "question": "What does 'perhaps you will give thanks' imply?", "turns_on": "Hope from the human viewpoint versus divine purpose, and why gratitude is framed as hope.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q53/p1", "position": "It is human-oriented hope, since literal uncertainty cannot apply to God.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya and Abu Hayyan locate the expectation with recipients of guidance."}, {"id": "2:185/q53/p2", "position": "It means God's purpose that people give thanks.", "reasons": "Tabari makes la'alla purposive; al-Kashshaf treats the hope as divine intent."}, {"id": "2:185/q53/p3", "position": "Gratitude is hoped for because sincere inner gratitude is less certain than outward fasting and takbir.", "reasons": "Tabatabai distinguishes outward magnification from sincerely leaving desire; Abu Hayyan observes hard duties end in hoped piety while concessions end in hoped gratitude."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q54", "question": "What inward meanings are given to this verse?", "turns_on": "The allegorical reading of Ramadan, witnessing, illness, ease, completion and praise.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q54/p1", "position": "Ramadan and fasting describe purification from sin, ego and heedlessness.", "reasons": "Sulami says witnessing God means fasting every moment from disobedience; Qushayri says mercy burns sins and reality burns ego-forms."}, {"id": "2:185/q54/p2", "position": "The month is the soul burning in divine light and witnessing the Essence.", "reasons": "Qashani reads sick people as veiled hearts and travelers as those still passing through stations; completion is their successive realization."}, {"id": "2:185/q54/p3", "position": "Ease is union by divine power and completion is a pure final state.", "reasons": "Qashani opposes the weak self's strain; Qushayri urges gratitude through a faithful final breath."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q55", "question": "What Ramadan virtues and events are reported?", "turns_on": "Different reports describe its nights, reward, worship and mercy.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q55/p1", "position": "The month brings opened Paradise, closed Hell, restrained devils, and a superior night.", "reasons": "Abu Hurayra reports variations; Tha'labi adds nightly release from Fire and angelic prayer."}, {"id": "2:185/q55/p2", "position": "Fasting and night worship bring forgiveness and exceptional reward.", "reasons": "Salman's sermon gives multiplied deeds, patience, charity and provision; other reports promise forgiveness, accepted supplication and reward even for feeding a faster with water or a date."}, {"id": "2:185/q55/p3", "position": "Its beginning is mercy, middle forgiveness, and end release from Fire.", "reasons": "Salman's sermon and Elmalili's cited report give this sequence."}, {"id": "2:185/q55/p4", "position": "Other reports praise Ramadan umra, prayer, and the fasting person's ordinary acts.", "reasons": "Qurtubi reports umra equal to Hajj; reports say the faster's sleep is worship, silence glorification and prayers answered."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q56", "question": "How does the verse connect with the surrounding fasting passage and later verses?", "turns_on": "One coherent explanation versus stages of legislation; fasting's purposes and the next prayer verse.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q56/p1", "position": "It specifies the earlier counted days, obligation and concession within a coherent passage.", "reasons": "Akhfash and Ibn Ashur link it to 2:184; Tabatabai says the three verses form one discourse, and al-Kashshaf assigns completion, takbir and gratitude to the respective provisions."}, {"id": "2:185/q56/p2", "position": "The closing praise prepares for God's nearness and answered prayer in the next verse.", "reasons": "Razi says praise precedes supplication, comparing Abraham's sequence in 26:78-83."}, {"id": "2:185/q56/p3", "position": "The hoped gratitude links the concession with earlier thanks for provision and with piety in 2:183.", "reasons": "Elmalili connects Eid thanksgiving to 2:172; al-Harali makes gratitude the later stage after taqwa."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q57", "question": "What does the Qur'an's revelation show about its form and recitation?", "turns_on": "The relation of its Arabic expression, reading, transmission and inimitability.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q57/p1", "position": "Its Arabic eloquence has a distinctive inimitable form.", "reasons": "Baqillani rejects Mani's and Ibn al-Muqaffa's putative rivals as sorcery, common wisdom or confused text; Arabic expressive forms are not all reproduced in translation."}, {"id": "2:185/q57/p2", "position": "Its transmitted recitation permits dialectal modes while preserving exact letters.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazari links seven modes to ease for varied Arab dialects and requires correct articulation according to ability."}, {"id": "2:185/q57/p3", "position": "Its recitation brings merit and requires reflection.", "reasons": "Suyuti reports letter rewards, intercession and criticism of rushed recitation without responding to glad tidings and warnings."}]}
{"id": "2:185/q58", "question": "If Eid is learned after the prayer time, may its prayer be held the next day?", "turns_on": "Whether the Eid prayer's time is fixed like other voluntary prayers or an established report permits a delayed celebration.", "positions": [{"id": "2:185/q58/p1", "position": "The Eid prayer may be held on the next morning when late crescent testimony made the original time impossible.", "reasons": "The report of Anas's uncles says the Prophet ordered breaking the fast and Eid prayer the next day; Qurtubi prefers following this established exception. {"id": "2:200/q01", "question": "What does qaḍaytum mean here?", "turns_on": "Whether qaḍāʾ describes completing one's own act or beginning it.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q01/p1", "position": "To perform and bring the rites to completion.", "reasons": "Wahidi explains discharge of what was due with 2:117 and 62:10; Razi distinguishes completion of one's act from imposing another's and informing; Qurtubi and Abu Hayyan distinguish later performance of missed worship; Ibn Qutayba and Zajjaj derive sealing and finishing, citing 4:103 and 46:29."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q02", "question": "What are the manāsik completed here?", "turns_on": "Whether the word denotes all Hajj acts, the sacrifice in particular, or ritual places with their acts understood.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q02/p1", "position": "All the rites and acts of worship of Hajj.", "reasons": "Zajjaj, Hasan, Ata and Ibn Atiyya take the whole pilgrimage; Ibn Atiyya prefers this and says Arafat marks a common completion point. Wahidi, Razi, Tabrisi and Ibn Ashur explain mansak as a verbal noun plural because worship has many acts and utterances; 2:128 is a parallel. The Prophet's instruction to learn his rites supports it for Qurtubi."}, {"id": "2:200/q02/p2", "position": "The sacrificial animals or slaughter and shedding of blood.", "reasons": "Tabari argues nasaka can describe slaughter and mansak is patterned like mashriq and maghrib; Tha'labi and Baghawi repeat the lexical point. Mujahid consistently glosses shedding blood; the sacrifice is the end of Hajj in Study Quran."}, {"id": "2:200/q02/p3", "position": "The ritual places, with the acts performed there understood.", "reasons": "Wahidi, Razi, Tabrisi, Abu Hayyan and Ibn Ashur supply an omitted noun, 'acts of the places'; mansak may name a place of worship or slaughter."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q03", "question": "How is manāsikakum pronounced and formed?", "turns_on": "Whether adjacent kāfs are pronounced separately or assimilated.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q03/p1", "position": "The two kāfs are pronounced distinctly by most readers.", "reasons": "Nahhas compares their separability with mandatory assimilation in 4:78; Samin says the inflectional vowel is normally preserved. Burhan and Itqan say the adjacent kāf pair without another letter occurs only here and in mā salakakum."}, {"id": "2:200/q03/p2", "position": "Abu Amr, especially al-Susi, assimilates the first kāf into the second.", "reasons": "Tha'labi and Qurtubi give identity of consonants as the reason; Samin says the inflectional vowel is treated as a stem vowel and removed, unlike examples in 9:35 and 3:106."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q04", "question": "When does the commanded remembrance occur relative to Hajj?", "turns_on": "Whether qaḍaytum and the following fa put remembrance after completion or allow it during the rites.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q04/p1", "position": "After the rites are finished, especially at Mina after the Aqaba stoning.", "reasons": "Razi says qaḍāʾ signals completion and fa makes it consequent; Abu Hayyan adds the preceding fa. Ibn Ashur places it after departure from Muzdalifa and describes Aqaba stoning, sacrifice and ifada; Itqan identifies the later remembrance of 2:203 with stoning on Tashriq days. Baghawi locates the pilgrim at Mina."}, {"id": "2:200/q04/p2", "position": "The command can apply during the rites, at Arafat, the Sacred Monument, circumambulation, and saʿy.", "reasons": "Jishumi reports this alongside after-completion; Razi rejects it because qaḍāʾ denotes completion; Abu Hayyan rejects the beginning-of-Hajj reading because of completion and fa."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q05", "question": "Which Hajj practices are connected with the close of the rites?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q05/p1", "position": "A pilgrim stones Aqaba on the Day of Sacrifice, then sacrifices and performs ifada; only sex remains forbidden.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur places Aqaba stoning between sunrise and noon on the tenth and reports scholarly agreement on the sequence."}, {"id": "2:200/q05/p2", "position": "The talbiya ceases at Mina on reaching and casting the first pebble; other stopping points are also reported.", "reasons": "Jishumi reports Malik's alternatives for a resident: after Arafat, touching the Black Stone, or seeing the House."}, {"id": "2:200/q05/p3", "position": "Arafah is a day of eating, drinking and takbir, so pilgrims should not fast.", "reasons": "Durr transmits Ibn Abbas's advice to men and women."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q06", "question": "What kind of remembrance does the command specify?", "turns_on": "Whether it is a particular pilgrimage formula, supplication, or continuing worship and praise.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q06/p1", "position": "Broad remembrance of God: praise, thanks, magnification, monotheism, obedience and worship.", "reasons": "Tabari prefers obedience and humility and links takbir in 2:203; Zajjaj calls for tawhid and recounting blessings; Ibn Ashur says worship in deed, speech and belief. Razi says these readings converge on constant remembrance and seeking needs from God."}, {"id": "2:200/q06/p2", "position": "Takbir on the days of Mina or after prayers on Sacrifice and Tashriq days.", "reasons": "Tabari links it to 2:203 as the newly prescribed remembrance; Razi says no other specific formula follows Hajj and notes disagreement on its timing; Itqan identifies Aqaba stoning and 2:203's Tashriq stoning."}, {"id": "2:200/q06/p3", "position": "All supplications at the sacred stations.", "reasons": "Mawardi, Wahidi, Jishumi and Tabrisi report this; Tabrisi says prayer there is better than elsewhere. Razi links it to humility, forgiveness after hardship, travel and expense, as with prayer after ṣalāt."}, {"id": "2:200/q06/p4", "position": "Invocation over the sacrificial animal.", "reasons": "Razi and Abu Hayyan report this as a specific reading tied to the completed sacrifice."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q07", "question": "Why is remembrance commanded after the rites?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q07/p1", "position": "To displace idle ancestral boasting and sustain gratitude and worship when worshippers might relax after Hajj.", "reasons": "Biqai and Tabatabai note the risk of forgetfulness after completion; Ibn Ashur links the renewed command with forgiveness and prevention of argument; Elmalılı says Hajj's awakening should continue and expose human frailty and worldly transience."}, {"id": "2:200/q07/p2", "position": "To move from bodily service in the rites to lifelong heartful love and remembrance.", "reasons": "Qushayri reads the transition inwardly as the body's duty followed by the heart's."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q08", "question": "What pre-Islamic practice occasioned the comparison with fathers?", "turns_on": "Reports differ on the practice and its location.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q08/p1", "position": "Pilgrims boasted of ancestors after Hajj at Mina, sometimes between its mosque and mountain.", "reasons": "Reports list feeding, kinship, blood money, war, hospitality, wealth, lineages, verse and prose. Muqatil and Farra place them between mosque and mountain; Qatada describes circles at Mina; Ibn Abbas describes all-day recitation. Many sources relate the same custom. Zajjaj repeats the mosque-and-mountain setting; Ibn al-Zubayr says boasting followed completed Hajj."}, {"id": "2:200/q08/p2", "position": "Pilgrims recalled ancestral deeds at the Jamrah or the House.", "reasons": "Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash locates it by the House; Mujahid, Ibn Atiyya and later reports place it at the jamrah. These are distinct location reports within the same practice."}, {"id": "2:200/q08/p3", "position": "Pilgrims recalled ancestral deeds while standing at Arafat.", "reasons": "Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima transmit this location."}, {"id": "2:200/q08/p4", "position": "Some Arabs habitually swore 'by your father' when speaking.", "reasons": "Al-Hasan transmits this distinct occasion; Ibn al-Anbari and Razi relate its religious significance, with a prophetic prohibition on such oaths."}, {"id": "2:200/q08/p5", "position": "At Mina a person asked God for the wealth and status his father possessed.", "reasons": "Al-Suddi's account says he spoke of his father's tent, bowl and wealth while neglecting God; other transmitters similarly connect the prayer with remembered fathers."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q09", "question": "What is the comparison to remembering fathers asking believers to do?", "turns_on": "Whether the model is the former boastful custom, a child's dependence, parental care, reverence or defense.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q09/p1", "position": "Replace the intensity of ancestral boasts with at least equal remembrance and praise of God.", "reasons": "Tabari's Anas report calls for praise, thanks and magnification; Zajjaj says their ancestral blessings came from God. Razi says false boasts merit punishment and true ones foster arrogance; Ibn Ashur says the comparison reproaches boastful idle talk rather than joining it to God's remembrance. Al-Qaffal's report of the Prophet at the conquest condemns tribal pride and cites 49:13. Nasafi compares Quraysh's ancestral remembrance, or that of a group surpassing them. Harali says the altered familiar formula follows a change of pilgrimage station."}, {"id": "2:200/q09/p2", "position": "Call on God constantly and dependently as

a small child calls for father and mother.", "reasons": "Ata describes a child's first babbling; other reports stress seeking help and refuge. Wahidi says fathers can name both parents as in 16:81. Asad says children see parents as goodness and power; Tabrisi prefers the ancestral boasting explanation."}, {"id": "2:200/q09/p3", "position": "Remember God as fathers remember their children.", "reasons": "Ikrima and Dahhak say parents are entrusted with their child; al-Qurazi's reading makes fathers the ones doing the remembering."}, {"id": "2:200/q09/p4", "position": "Defend God's sanctuary and honor against shirk as one defends family honor.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya's group and Qurtubi compare defending religion with defending ancestors; Qushayri extends the analogy to answering error and innovation; Biqai compares a son rejecting a partner for his father."}, {"id": "2:200/q09/p5", "position": "Venerate God rather than swear by fathers.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Anbari cites Arab oath practice; Razi cites the Prophet's command to swear by God or remain silent."}, {"id": "2:200/q09/p6", "position": "Remember and acknowledge God as people acknowledge their fathers or their favors.", "reasons": "Ibn Jawzi records acknowledgment and remembered kindness; Abu Muslim stresses never forgetting one's benefactor; Razi reports a monotheistic analogy of affirming God's oneness as one affirms ancestors."}, {"id": "2:200/q09/p7", "position": "Be more indignant at disobedience to God than at an insult to one's parents.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas says the comparison is not daily mention of fathers but loyalty expressed by anger on God's behalf."}, {"id": "2:200/q09/p8", "position": "Revere God as one reveres an honored person, while recognizing God's greater claim.", "reasons": "Harali warns that attachment to visible people can make God's status seem merely human; Biqai cites 'be ashamed before God as before a dignified man' as an analogy."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q10", "question": "Why does the verse name fathers rather than mothers?", "turns_on": "Whether fathers denote reverence specifically or stand for both parents.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q10/p1", "position": "Fathers are remembered with reverence; mothers with compassion.", "reasons": "Qushayri says God is revered and shows mercy rather than receiving mercy."}, {"id": "2:200/q10/p2", "position": "Fathers stand for both parents in ordinary speech.", "reasons": "Wahidi, Razi and others compare 16:81, where clothing protecting from heat implies protection from cold; the child calls both father and mother."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q11", "question": "Why should remembrance of God exceed remembrance of fathers?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q11/p1", "position": "God is the ultimate source of the parents' virtues and every blessing, and has the greater claim.", "reasons": "Muqatil, Farra, Zajjaj and others trace ancestral good to God. Razi contrasts limited ancestral merits with God's endless perfections; Qushayri says parents raised one but God's favor is more complete. Biqai notes parents may also mislead. Tabatabai highlights divine guidance."}]}
{"id": "2:200/q12", "question": "What force has 'or stronger remembrance'?", "turns_on": "Whether it means more intense, more frequent, or both.", "positions": [{"id": "2:200/q12/p1", "position": "Remember God at least as intensely, indeed more intensely, than fathers.", "reasons": "Muqatil and Wahidi take the comparative literally.
